home.title: Transformer X-Ray
home.kicker: A CUDA course built on a real, running transformer
home.h1c: a GPT that thinks in your browser
home.lede: Twelve lessons from your first thread to a fused attention kernel. You write real CUDA, run it on a simulated GPU that shows every memory access, then watch the same kernel power a 1.8M-parameter language model.
home.proof2b: compiled and timed on real hardware
home.proof3b: The model, its gradients and its kernels are real and run live
home.canvasMem: the 32-byte sectors this load fetches, 8 floats each
home.pathTitle: The path: twelve lessons laid out like the chip
home.pathSub: Each block is a lesson. It lights up when your kernel passes its correctness check and its performance targets. Finish the row and you understand why the next row exists.
home.howSub: Every lesson follows the same loop, so after lesson two you stop thinking about the site and think about the GPU.
home.how1Body: A simulator built from the lesson's kernel. You drag the block size, watch warps form, and see memory transactions coalesce or shatter.
home.how2Body: Real CUDA in an editor. The in-browser GPU runs it warp by warp and reports sectors per request, bank conflicts, divergence and races, with the offending line highlighted.
home.how3Body: Jump to the inspector where this exact kernel runs inside the transformer, with its measured time on an RTX GPU.
home.labsSub: The model is live on every page. When a lesson mentions a tensor, you can go hover its numbers.
home.labPlayBody: Prompt it, then click any character to see the 65-way distribution it was sampled from.
home.labTrainBody: Start from noise. Watch loss fall at three steps a second, then x-ray the half-trained weights.
home.labInspectBody: Nine views from tokens to AdamW, each with a forward and a backward twin.
home.footer1: Transformer X-Ray. Open source, runs entirely in your browser.
home.howNote: The simulators, the editor and the in-browser GPU open with the next release. The model and the three labs are live today.
